subject: SLO mapping + deployment questions for Quantiscale — follow-up
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@quantiscale.ai>, dev-support@quantiscale.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 Feb 2028 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: SLO mapping + deployment questions for Quantiscale — follow-up

Hi Asha — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick post-call note to capture what we heard and the immediate asks so we can move toward a technical proposal.

Key pain / goals you flagged
- Predictable 95th-percentile latency under 350ms for single-turn text generation at 512 tokens for the customer-facing API.
- Sustained throughput target ~220 requests/sec during daytime peak (US East), with small bursts to 400 rps for sales events.
- Data residency: customer data must stay in your VPC (private deployment) and PrismaBank compliance requires audit logs retained for 13 months.
- Cost sensitivity: want to keep per-request infra costs under $0.015 after optimization.

Technical constraints we noted
- Model: running an open LLM base (Quantiscale uses Q-Transformer-7B) with custom fine-tunes for completion and reranking. KV cache persists per-session.
- Typical input length: median 120 tokens; 99th percentile ~680 tokens due to conversation history.
- Burst pattern: diurnal peak centered 14:00–17:00 ET, periodic marketing-triggered surges.

Immediate asks / next steps I promised
1) I attached a starter capacity worksheet (quantiscale_capacity_model.xlsx) — please drop your real QPS per region and 95/99 token distribution into the green tab; we’ll snap numbers into a topology recommendation.
2) We’ll propose two topology options: (A) Dedicated VPC deployment with autoscaling GPU pool + hot KV cache; (B) Hybrid: hosted control plane + customer-managed GPU nodes in your VPC. I put a short draft topology doc in the attachments (redwood_deploy_topology_v1.pdf).
3) We need sample traces or a small request trace CSV (20–50 requests) showing token lengths and latencies for current infra so we can validate kernel selection and batching strategy.
4) Call to decide: a 45-minute deep dive with your infra and SRE folks next week — can you do Tue 2028-03-05 11:00 ET or Wed 2028-03-06 14:00 ET?

Notes on what we’ll evaluate in the deep dive
- Batch sizing and KV cache hit-rate impact on p95 latency
- Quantization / model variant trade-offs for cost targets
- Autoscaling warm-up and cold-start mitigation strategies for burst events
- Audit log forwarding and retention architecture for 13-month compliance

If you’d like, we can redact customer PII in any traces you share before sending.

Thanks — attaching the worksheet and short topology sketch.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0163

Attachments: quantiscale_capacity_model.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood_deploy_topology_v1.pdf (PDF)
From: Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@quantiscale.ai>

Date: Mon, 27 Feb 2028 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLO mapping + deployment questions for Quantiscale — follow-up

Thanks Karthik — great summary, appreciate capturing the asks. I dropped a first-pass data export into the green tab of the workbook (anonymized). The CSV traces you requested are attached to this reply (we compressed to trace_sample_02.csv.gz).

Couple of clarifications:
- The model is a Quantiscale fork (Q-Transformer-7B-ft) with tokenizer differences; we expect the tokenization overhead to shift token counts +5–8% versus standard tiktoken.
- For KV cache, sessions are keyed to user_id and stick for up to 48 hours. Hit-rate is ~82% during normal hours, drops to ~60% during marketing surges.
- Audit logs are exported to our S3, and we can configure a cross-account sink into an audited bucket in your VPC if required.

We can do Tue 2028-03-05 11:00 ET — I’ll pull in our SRE lead (Dev Patel) and product ops.

Asha
VP Product, Quantiscale
asha.reddy@quantiscale.ai
Attachments: trace_sample_02.csv.gz (gzip CSV)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@quantiscale.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Feb 2028 08:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLO mapping + deployment questions for Quantiscale — follow-up

Perfect — thanks for the sample traces and the workbook feed. We looked through the anonymized traces this morning. High-level findings pre-deep-dive:

Preliminary sizing notes (ballpark)
- Given median 120 tokens and 99th ~680 with your tokenizer delta, plan for an effective 99th token of ~730 for kernel selection and memory.
- For p95 < 350ms at 220 rps: a single pool of A100/80GB-equivalent GPUs with continuous batching and a hot KV service will likely meet the SLO, assuming 80% cache hit-rate; if hit-rate drops to 60% during surges, we should add a small warm pool to keep p95 within target.
- To hit the per-request cost target (~$0.015), we’ll test a quantized int8 variant and evaluate throughput uplift; one or two model variants (fp16 and int8) mitigates regression risk.

Topology suggestions attached in redwood_deploy_topology_v1.pdf — highlights:
- Option A (Recommended for compliance): Private deployment inside your VPC. Control plane still managed by Redwood but audit logs and metrics forwarded to your S3. Autoscale policy with target concurrency-based scaling and a 4-minute warm window for GPU spin-up.
- Option B (Faster time-to-value): Hybrid where inference runs on Redwoods' dedicated capacity but all traffic egress is tunneled through your VPC for audit logs. Simpler but slightly higher per-unit cost.

Prep for Tue 11:00 ET
- Ask Dev Patel/SRE to join with one sample instance (can be dev sandbox) and confirm whether the environment can expose Prometheus metrics + p95 traces over the demo.
- We will run a short live load test (10 min) with a subset of the sample trace to observe p95 behavior with and without KV hits. Please confirm a small service account we can use to push test traffic.

Marissa and Connor — would you plan to join the call? If so, I’ll send the calendar invite with a pre-call checklist.

Thanks — I’ll prepare an agenda and test harness notes and share ahead of the meeting.

Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Adding a quick ops checklist in-line so we don’t forget items during the call:
- Dev service account credentials (scoped) for load test — who manages provisioning? (Asha / Quantiscale)
- Prometheus scrape endpoints and a sample prometheus.yml or endpoint URL
- Confirm region (you said US East; please confirm if this is us-east1 or us-east-2)
- Tokenization sample: please add a 50-request tokenization CSV so we can reproduce the +5–8% delta locally
- Audit log schema sample and S3 bucket role to accept cross-account writes

I’ll slot into Tue 11:00 ET and will prepare the load-test harness and a short checklist doc (link will be shared in the invite). Connor will own the test runner and Marissa will coordinate the meeting logistics (note: Marissa is me — coordinating).

See you Tue — Marissa
